ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, point $E$ is the incenter of $\triangle ABC$. The extension line of $AE$ intersects the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$ at point $D$. Connect $BE$. If $\angle CBD = 34^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle BEC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}:\\
Since $\angle CBD=34^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle CAD=34^\circ$,\\
since point E is the incenter of $\triangle ABC$,\\
it follows that $\angle BAC=2\angle CAD=68^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle EBC+\angle ECB=(180^\circ-68^\circ)\div 2=56^\circ$,\\
hence, $\angle BEC=180^\circ-56^\circ=\boxed{124^\circ}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution}:\\ Since $\angle CBD=34^\circ$,\\ it follows that $\angle CAD=34^\circ$,\\ since point E is the incenter of $\triangle ABC$,\\ it follows that $\angle BAC=2\angle CAD=68^\circ$,\\ therefore $\angle EBC+\angle ECB=(180^\circ-68^\circ)\div 2=56^\circ$,\\ hence, $\angle BEC=180^\circ-56^\circ=\boxed{124^\circ}$
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, the four points A, B, C, D are on the same circle, A is at the upper right, B is at the lower left, C is on the right side, D is below; E is located inside triangle ABC, and is on the straight line AD, BE is connected in the figure, and what is required is ∠BEC. The problem gives that E is the incenter of △ABC, and the extension line of AE intersects the circumcircle at D, and it is known that ∠CBD = 34°.

Reasoning: Because A, B, C, D are concyclic, ∠CBD and ∠CAD are both inscribed angles, and they both subtend the same arc CD, so ∠CAD = ∠CBD = 34°. Also because E is the incenter of △ABC, AE is the angle bisector of ∠BAC; at the same time A, E, D are collinear, therefore ∠CAD is ∠CAE, that is, half of ∠BAC. So ∠BAC = 2 × 34° = 68°. The incenter angle property gives ∠BEC = 90° + 1/2∠BAC = 90° + 34° = 124°.
